C.1.2 Scope of Work The Contractor must provide operations and maintenance support for the NIMS/CMIS system, provide quality assurance and quality control, provide security compliance and ensure uninterrupted system availability. This effort also requires the vendor to serve as a SME and provide support with system architecture, software recommendations, system design, development, testing, deployment, and documentation for a new system to support NISC V contract requirements when required. Contractor will maintain NIMS/CMIS security certifications required to operate the software and its associated server hardware. The Contractor must also provide transition support to any potential new vendor at the contract’s end. C.1.3 Objectives The objectives of the NEST’s Scope of Work are to provide the following support: • Operation and Maintenance of the NIMS/CMIS System: o Enhancement to NIMS systems, KITT Financial Database (KFDB) reporting database, and NISC Invoice Approval Tool (NIAT) using existing technology stack to support business process requirements as and when required by NISC PMO; 693KA9-26-R-00003 Part I – The Schedule Section C – Statement of Work 7

certifications_partner.text: ational response to the changing needs of the manufacturing sector which is driven by the need to adopt industry 4.0 technologies and practices in the face of both Brexit and global competition challenges. The centre will also provide training through apprenticeships and traineeships for people who are interested in pursuing careers in the advance manufacturing domain. It is envisaged that the centre will become a focal point for the delivery of upskilling and reskilling opportunities for the manufacturing sector. entity_geography.text: Performance Successful performance will be an essential feature of work awarded under the Panel. Poor performance will be identified and raised with panel members and may result in termination of a contract and/or removal from the panel. Evaluation Criteria for Admittance to the Panel Application Requirements The Contracting Authority is using a process similar to the OPEN procedure for the establishment of this panel, therefore, while all interested parties may apply, only those demonstrating that they have the required level of qualifications, experience and technical capacity will have their application considered. In order to demonstrate eligibility, applicants are required to provide the following information: General Information Including the following information: Name of applicant Address Key contact name Key contact email Key contact phone / mobile Website if applicable Other social media platform activities Date of establishment Insurance Requirements Confirmation of insurances in place and commitment to put the following levels in place if successful for the contract: Must provide evidence of this level of cover being in place or a letter from an Insurance company stating that these levels of cover may be put in place if a contract is awarded within one week of the appointment

THE PROVISION OF PROJECT ADVISORY SERVICES UNDER THE ERASMUS+ AND THE EUROPEAN SOLIDARITY CORPS PROGRAMMES FOR THE EUROPEAN UNION PROGRAMMES AGENCY (EUPA) Reference is made to the above -captioned public call for tenders for which the deadline for submission of offers is 16th October 2026 at 09:30 hrs. Below please find a set of clarifications, which are construed to form an integral part of the tender document. Question 1 Estimate Quantity in Hours Per Year If I don't complete the hours estimated in the Financial bid, do these go over to the following year? Answer 1 As per Tender dossier: - Section 3 – Terms of Reference - 3) Assumptions and Risks - 3.2) Risks (a) The number of working hours per month may vary according to the needs that might arise. As per Financial Bid form template, the estimate quantity in hours per year is 250 hours. Question 2 Preparation work and Online support! Does preparation work before the meetings count as work? Does online application support count as work? Does online application support count as work? Question 3 Estimated number of hours If I don't finish the estimated number of hours in 3 years, does the contract end? what will happen? Answer 3 The Contract shall be for a period of three (3) years – 36 months. All other documents, conditions and requirements, which are not superseded by this Clarification, remain in place. Waterford and Wexford Education and Training Board (WWETB) provides a comprehensive range of education and training services throughout Waterford and Wexford and is the largest education and training provider in counties Waterford and Wexford. WWETB’s educational and training provision includes second-level schools, primary school, further education colleges and a range of adult and further education centres delivering education and training programmes, Post Leaving Certificate Courses (PLCs), Youthreach centres, Outdoor Education and Youth Services. WWETB places learning and the learner at the heart of its educational provision. For more information on WWETB and ETBI go to http://waterfordwexford.etb.ie/ and www.etbi.ie For more information on ETBs and ETBI go to www.etbi.ie See Appendix 4 for details of all schools and centres under WWETB remit. Panel members will be required to send in up to-date tax and insurance information on an annual basis to remain on the panel. Indicative Budget The estimated total value of purchases pursuant to this contract may be in the region of €65,000 to €221,000 (ex. VAT) over the lifetime of the agreement.
